correctness.rationale: In generalized theta graph Theta(ell_1,...,ell_d) with d>=3 paths ell_i>=2, the branch vertices have equal round colors by the graph involution and are distinguished from degree-2 internal vertices at round 1. For internal position i on a length ell path, equality of round-r colors is exactly equality of unordered clipped distances {min(i,r),min(ell-i,r)}, proved inductively using the two neighbor colors plus branch marker. Within a longest length L, positions unresolved after round r force r>=floor(L/2). Across distinct lengths a<b, the shorter path tip first differs at round a; the largest such shorter length is second-largest DISTINCT path length S, requiring r>=S. These conditions jointly suffice: each path position is distinguished up to its reversal and shorter-length distance sums differ from every longer clipped pair. Hence Stab=max(floor(L/2),S). At fixed d and n=sum ell_i-d+2, L<=n-d and distinct second length S<=floor((n-d+1)/2); d-2 paths of length 2 and two balanced lengths attain upper bound. Independent direct refinement for 2,958 nondecreasing length tuples d=3..6, ell=2..9 matched the depth formula, corroborating but not proving its infinite quantification.
